## LMDI emissions decomposition tool, in the browser. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/carbon-bridge/

Four causes for one change in emissions, with nothing left over. Eighteen figures across three products and two years, and the residual is computed on every redraw.

Case study · esg-toolkit 

## Emissions decomposition
 Four causes for one change in emissions, with nothing left over.
 Running here Emissions decomposition Open full size Emissions decomposition Eighteen figures, three products across two years. Change any one of them and the four effects, the chart and the residual are computed again.

### Problem
 A company that made less of a dirty product and more of a clean one while its suppliers changed underneath it has four stories running at once, and changing one factor at a time leaves a remainder that belongs to none of them and can be argued in either direction. 

### Method
 The logarithmic mean Divisia index in its additive form, LMDI-I, where a segment's emissions are total output times its share of output times its energy per unit times its emissions per unit of energy, each factor takes a share of the change weighted by the logarithmic mean of the segment's emissions in the two periods, and there is no residual term at all. 

### What it does
 A waterfall of six bars, the base year total, the four effects in order and the target year total, and under it the check: the four effects to six decimal places, their sum, the observed difference between the two years, and the residual in exponential notation. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses to hide the residual: LMDI-I leaves none analytically, so that line carries floating point noise in exponential notation on every redraw and would report a broken identity before anything else did. 
 It refuses to run without output, so where total output is zero or below in either period it prints that total output must be above zero in both and draws nothing. 
 It refuses negative inputs, reading a negative number typed into any of the eighteen fields as zero, because it would put a logarithm outside its domain and return four effects that are all NaN. 
 It refuses to pass off a substitution as a result: values at or below zero are replaced by 1e-12 before the logarithms are taken, which is a numerical convenience and not a finding. 
 It refuses to draw the chart from zero and say nothing, so the scale is computed from the values it has to show and a line under the waterfall states the range it runs over. 
 It refuses to explain: the four numbers say how much of the change sits with output, mix, energy intensity and the emission factor, and they name no cause. 

### In closing
 I wanted a bridge chart whose numbers could not be moved by whoever happened to be drawing it. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/esg-toolkit 
 Notes

## Discounted cash flow calculator, free in the browser. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/dcf-lab/

A discounted cash flow where the terminal value is not allowed to hide. Two sliders, the cost of capital and terminal growth, and every figure follows them.

Case study · analyst-toolkit 

## Discounted cash flow
 A discounted cash flow where the terminal value is not allowed to hide.
 Running here Discounted cash flow Open full size Discounted cash flow Two sliders, the cost of capital and terminal growth. The headline share, the bar, the five year table and the line of arithmetic all follow them.

### Problem
 A discounted cash flow puts its answer in one cell, the perpetuity after the last forecast year is often the larger half of it, and setting terminal growth at or above the cost of capital still returns a number the spreadsheet is happy to print. 

### Method
 Five forecast cash flows discounted on the end year convention, a Gordon growth perpetuity taken at the end of year five and brought back with the same year five discount factor, and a headline that is the share of the enterprise value the perpetuity contributes. 

### What it does
 Two sliders, and every movement recomputes the headline share, one bar split between forecast and terminal present value, a table of the five years with their discount factors, and one line of arithmetic with its numbers substituted in. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses to value a perpetuity that grows at or faster than the rate discounting it, and prints Refused in place of an enterprise value, because such a perpetuity has unbounded value. 
 It refuses the usual repair of clamping growth to just under the cost of capital, because the clamp swaps in a different model whose answer runs away as the clamp tightens. 
 The refusal is narrow: the five forecast years still discount normally, and it is only the perpetuity that has no answer. 
 It refuses to be a valuation, so there is no net debt, no share count, no currency, no per share figure, and the cash flows cannot be edited. 

### In closing
 I built this because the argument in a valuation is usually about the forecast years, and the answer usually is not. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/analyst-toolkit 
 Notes

## CBAM embedded emissions calculator, free. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/embedded/

A single embedded emissions figure hides the one thing an abatement decision needs. Twenty figures across four processes, recomputed until the reconciliation closes.

Case study · esg-toolkit 

## CBAM embedded emissions
 A single embedded emissions figure hides the one thing an abatement decision needs.
 Running here CBAM embedded emissions Open full size CBAM embedded emissions Twenty figures across four processes. Resolving recomputes the embedded emissions of each and closes on the reconciliation.

### Problem
 Embedded emissions for anything made in stages are a chain traced backwards, crude steel carrying pig iron and pig iron carrying coke and sintered ore, and the finished figure cannot say whether the carbon came out of the coke oven or the blast furnace, which is what an abatement decision turns on; attribute by the immediate supplier and coke, reached down two paths, is counted twice. 

### Method
 Processes are resolved in dependency order by a depth first walk with a visiting set, every entry is keyed by the process that released the emissions rather than by the intermediate it arrived through, so a shared input accumulates into one entry, and direct and indirect are carried as a pair the whole way down and never summed. 

### What it does
 Four processes with every figure editable, activity level, attributed direct emissions, electricity and the quantity of each precursor consumed, and resolving prints the specific embedded emissions of each process direct and indirect side by side, a bar per releasing process, and the reconciliation of the attribution against the figure it attributes. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses a precursor whose emissions nobody stated, because an input with no source process inside the installation needs supplier data or a default value from the current implementing act, and a button on the page empties that field so the refusal can be seen. 
 It refuses to merge direct and indirect into a total, because that is how they are reported to the authority, the certificate calculation does not treat them alike, and a number that collapses them loses what nothing downstream can recover. 
 It refuses to iterate a cycle: where two processes each name the other as a precursor the chain has no bottom, so the instrument prints the loop by name and stops. 

### In closing
 A declaration needs one number and this produces it, and the rest of the page exists because that number tells a declarant what to report and an engineer nothing at all about where to spend. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/esg-toolkit 
 Notes

## Marginal abatement cost curve tool, free. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/marginal-abatement/

An abatement cost curve that prints the arithmetic behind every bar. One carbon price decides which measures clear, how much they abate and what the set costs.

Case study · esg-toolkit 

## Marginal abatement cost curve
 An abatement cost curve that prints the arithmetic behind every bar.
 Running here Marginal abatement cost curve Open full size Marginal abatement cost curve One slider, a carbon price from nothing to 200 EUR a tonne. Which measures clear, how much they abate and what the set costs all follow it.

### Problem
 Boiler tuning at 12 thousand euro returning 3.6 thousand a year for four years and rooftop solar at 620 thousand returning 74 thousand a year for twenty five cannot be ranked by their price tags, because one is spent once and the other returns every year the equipment lasts, and neither is worth anything until it is set against a price. 

### Method
 A marginal abatement cost curve built on the levelised cost of abatement: the capital cost becomes an equivalent annual amount through a capital recovery factor over that measure's own life, the annual saving comes off it, and what remains is divided by the tonnes abated each year, cheapest first, ties broken by name. 

### What it does
 One slider from 0 to 200 EUR a tonne in steps of 1, starting at 12, with three readouts following it, how many of the ten measures clear, their cumulative annual abatement against the total available and the net annual cost of the set, and selecting any bar opens its arithmetic under the chart. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses to let the discount rate be argued: eight percent sits in the code, once, for every measure, because a curve whose reader can move the rate can be rearranged until it agrees with a decision already taken. 
 It refuses to give a cost without the arithmetic, so selecting a bar prints the capital recovery factor to six places and the division that produced the cost per tonne, carrying that measure's own capex, saving, life and abatement. 
 It refuses to hide the half of the curve that lies below zero: five of the ten measures pay for themselves at the stated discount rate, and their bars are drawn under the zero line rather than clipped away. 
 It refuses to pretend the measures were modelled against each other, so every cost comes from that measure's own row, the totals are plain sums, and the code contains no interaction term. 
 It refuses to be a business case: no payback period, no net present value, no internal rate of return, no capital budget, and the one money figure is the net annual cost of the selected set at the levelised cost. 
 It refuses to show an empty answer as a zero, so below the cheapest measure it names the price at which the curve starts and shows the three cheapest measures anyway. 

### In closing
 A cost curve is a ranking, and this one prints the arithmetic of its ranking so that the argument can be about the inputs. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/esg-toolkit 
 Notes

## Market sizing calculator, top down and bottom up. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/market-sizer/

Two sizings and the gap between them. Four top down factors against nine bottom up drivers, because one number arrived at one way is not evidence of anything.

Case study · analyst-toolkit 

## Market sizing
 Two sizings, the gap between them, and what each assumption would have to become.
 Running here Market sizing Open full size Market sizing Thirteen figures, four top down factors and nine bottom up drivers. The gap, and what each assumption would have to become, follow them.

### Problem
 A market is sized twice, top down as a universe narrowed by shares and bottom up as a sum of segments, and the disagreement between the two is the only quantity in the exercise nobody assumed, which averaging them throws away. 

### Method
 Top down against bottom up, reconciled by inversion rather than by judgement: the instrument takes each assumption in turn, holds every other assumption still, and computes the value that one assumption would have to take for the two totals to agree. 

### What it does
 Four top down factors and three bottom up segments of three drivers each, all editable, with the two totals, the gap and the gap as a percentage of the top down total above them, and one row per assumption giving its current value, the value it would have to take and the multiple between the two. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses to produce a market size, so there is no average, no midpoint, no range and no recommendation about which sizing to believe, because the difference is the finding. 
 It refuses to imply something impossible, so an implied share above 100 percent, or any negative implied value, is marked infeasible with the reason written out. 
 It refuses to scale a zero, because a factor sitting at zero cannot be multiplied into anything else, and the table says so in place of the implied column. 
 It refuses the impossible segment: where the other segments already sum past the top down total, every driver in the segment being solved is marked infeasible and the two figures that make it so are named. 
 It refuses negative and unreadable inputs, reading anything that does not parse as a number, or parses below zero, as zero. 
 It refuses to claim a market it has not measured, so every money figure is labelled EUR, illustrative, in both totals and in the readouts. 

### In closing
 The gap between two sizings is the most informative thing either of them produces. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/analyst-toolkit 
 Notes

## Climate data provenance checker, in the browser. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/provenance/

A figure that carries its source and keeps carrying it through the arithmetic. Take a mandatory field away and the refusal can be seen rather than described.

Case study · open-climate-data 

## Data provenance
 A figure that carries its source, and keeps carrying it through the arithmetic.
 Running here Data provenance Open full size Data provenance Two records with every field editable, and a button that takes a mandatory one away so the refusal can be seen rather than described.

### Problem
 A grid intensity of 412 gCO2e per kWh stored as a number cannot say which portal it came from, and a figure read in March from the 2024 edition is not the figure read in September after a restatement; a citation kept beside the number does not survive contact with a calculation either, because two sourced figures divided leave an ordinary float with the notes somewhere else. 

### Method
 A cited value is a magnitude, a unit and a lineage: five fields are mandatory on every record, identity is the hash of its canonical form with the timestamp normalised to UTC, merging two lineages is union over those identities, and the Python test suite sweeps that invariant over four hundred randomly generated arithmetic expression trees. 

### What it does
 Two records side by side with every field editable, a button that takes a mandatory field away so the refusal can be seen, an operation selector that combines them and prints the sources the result admits to, and an audit of what has gone stale, what has no address, what recorded no query and whether the licences have been mixed. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses to construct a record with a mandatory field missing, and there is a button on the page whose only job is to empty the licence field, because a described refusal is not the same as a seen one. 
 It refuses a timestamp with no timezone, because an instant with no offset is not an instant and assuming UTC would silently make two different retrievals identify as one. 
 It refuses to say whether two licences may be combined in a published figure: it names them and reports that they have been mixed, and the rest is a legal question with a jurisdiction attached. 

### In closing
 The claim any published figure makes rests on whether anybody can get back to where the number came from, and that is a property of how it was stored long before it is a property of how carefully it was quoted. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/open-climate-data 
 Notes

## Emissions reduction pathway calculator, free. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/target-path/

A reduction target is one number. The path to it decides how much carbon reaches the atmosphere, and four fields draw it with every chart and total following.

Case study · esg-toolkit 

## Reduction pathway
 A reduction target is one number. The path to it is where the carbon actually goes.
 Running here Reduction pathway Open full size Reduction pathway Four fields draw the path, and the two panels under it take figures of their own. Every chart, table and total recomputes.

### Problem
 Two companies can make the identical commitment, hit it on the same date and put very different quantities of carbon into the atmosphere on the way, because the atmosphere responds to the integral of the path: a linear path removes a fixed share of the base year every year and a compounding path a fixed share of last year, and progress reported against the base year flatters a company that is already behind. 

### Method
 Two pathway shapes, absolute contraction as a straight line and intensity convergence multiplied by the reader's own activity forecast, a budget taken as the area under the path by the trapezoid rule over one year steps, and a diagnostic that inverts the path to solve for the annual cut that still lands on the target. 

### What it does
 Four fields draw the path and the endpoint, the total reduction, the cumulative budget, a chart and a table of every year follow them; a second panel runs the same rate as a linear and a compounding path and prints the gap in percentage points and in extra carbon, and a third marks each reported actual behind or ahead and computes the rate required from the last year entered. 

### What it refuses to do
 It refuses to interpolate a year the reader left blank, and where the years entered are not consecutive the cumulative panel says so and withholds the total rather than computing one across a gap. 
 It refuses to present 4.2 percent as a rule: it is the floor the SBTi sets under the absolute contraction approach for a near term Scope 1 and 2 target, printed with its publisher and the date it was read, and the page makes neither the upward adjustment for base years later than 2020 nor the separate lower rate for Scope 3. 
 It refuses to call a target met, because nothing in the arithmetic knows whether the inventory held the same boundary two years running, whether the base year was recalculated after a disposal, or whether a reduction came from decarbonising or from selling the emitting part of the business. 

### In closing
 The tool exists for the two figures a spreadsheet does not print unless somebody thinks to ask for them: the area under the path, and the rate that delay has already made necessary. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/esg-toolkit 
 Notes

## Unit and dimension checker for emissions data. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/cases/unitguard/

A converter that names what is missing instead of guessing it. A spreadsheet will add a mass to an energy without a word; this one answers with a refusal.

Case study · unitguard 

## Unit conversion
 A converter that names what is missing instead of guessing it.
 Running here Unit conversion Open full size Unit conversion A quantity and two units, with four worked examples to load. Every change is answered with a conversion or with a refusal.

### Problem
 A spreadsheet will add a mass to an energy without a word, and the version of that failure specific to emissions work is the gas species: a tonne of methane and a tonne of carbon dioxide share nothing but mass, moving between them is a choice of assessment report and time horizon, and turning CO2e back into one gas asks for a mixture the figure was built to forget. 

### Method
 Dimensional analysis with the gas species carried inside the unit, magnitudes read as exact rationals over big integers rather than floating point, and a conversion allowed only where the dimensions match and, for gases, a route between the two species is defined. 

### What it does
 A quantity, two units and four worked examples as chips, answered either with Converted, the result and the sentence written out in full, or with Refused and the input that was missing; a result that does not terminate in decimal prints with a leading tilde, as five hundred tonnes of carbon to tCO2 does at 5500/3. 

### What it refuses to do
 Methane to CO2e, the refusal the instrument exists for: there is only a global warming potential, and over one hundred years AR4 puts methane at 25, AR5 at 28 and AR6 at 27.0 for biogenic and 29.8 for fossil methane, so the instrument names all of them and picks none. 
 CO2e back into a single gas, because tonnes of CO2 equivalent are a unit of account and without the mix that produced the figure there is no mass to return; the direction that does work is CO2 to CO2e, where the potential is 1 by definition. 
 A bare mass into a gas unit, because asking for t to tCO2 asks the instrument to supply the species, and the refusal tells you to state it on the input side. 
 A gas unit into a bare mass, which is arithmetically trivial and refused anyway, because dropping the species stops the figure from being an emissions figure at all. 
 Across dimensions: energy to mass is refused with both dimensions named and with the missing thing named too, an energy density or an emission factor, and the instrument carries no default emission factor for any country in any year. 
 Anything that is not a magnitude, answered with Not a number, and two species with no defined route between them, answered with Not defined. 

### In closing
 A converter that guesses is worse than no converter, because it returns a number, and numbers get believed. 

### Elsewhere
 github.com/Keremozdemirra/unitguard 
 Notes

## Colophon. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/colophon/

How this site is made: the type, the stack, the hosting, the licences, and what it does not do. No analytics, no cookies, no third party requests at all.

05 5   parts 

## How it is made.
 Everything on this page can be checked against the repository.

### Type
 Fraunces for display, Instrument Sans for text, IBM Plex Mono for figures and labels, all three under the SIL Open Font License and served from this domain. 

### Stack
 Next.js as a static export: no server, no database, no build-time secret. 

### Hosting
 GitHub Pages, from a public repository, where a push is a deploy. 

### What it does not do
 No analytics, no trackers, no request to a third party at any point, and the language you choose is remembered in your own browser and nowhere else. 

### Licences
 Third-party notices . The instruments and tools are open source; each repository names its licence.

## My life as a game. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/life/

A hand drawn game of one year in the life of a tree, with a museum buried under it and two cities either side. Drawn line by line, not photographed.

Interactive · three languages 

## My life as a game
 A hand drawn game of one year in the life of a single tree, with a museum under its roots, Istanbul on one side and Munich on the other.
 Play opens in a new tab Arrow keys scrub it. Space plays it. Scroll up from the cover and the sky opens. Made for a computer. Open this page on one and it plays here. 

### What it is
 Scrolling down runs a year, summer through the turn and the fall to dusk and then underground to the roots and the doors, with every leaf's flight calculated from your scroll position, so scrolling back up runs it exactly in reverse and the leaves return to their branches. 

### The world
 Scroll up and the sky opens, with clouds, a hot air balloon towing a banner, birds circling a thermal and at night the stars; drag sideways and the camera pans west to Istanbul, the Bosphorus, Kız Kulesi, a working ferry and the Beyazıt gate, or east to Munich, the Alps, the Frauenkirche, the Eisbach and its surfer, a beer garden, the U-Bahn and TUM. 
 Underground there is a cellar, a well whose rope reaches the water table, an ant colony with branching galleries, a mole, a sleeping rabbit, a buried amphora, an aquifer with a blind fish in it, and a museum of thirteen objects in three bands, the deepest being the earliest. 

### Six ways in
 The Beyazıt gate of the university in Istanbul, the U-Bahn stairs in Munich, the banner behind the balloon, the door of the house, a workbench with a saw leaning on it, and a game table with the stones of a game nobody finished still on the board. 

### How it is built
 One HTML file for the whole game, no framework, no images, no video, no tracking, and the tree, the roots and the grass are grown by a seeded random walk, so the same tree comes back every time. 
 Nothing publishes from its repository until an eleven gate audit passes, which blocks a release that carries a credential pattern or a personal data value, that leaves a string untranslated, or that ships a dictionary which is not symmetric across the three languages. One gate rebuilds every page, one reads each built page back as JavaScript, and one refuses a CV older than the page it was printed from. 

### Where it lives
 It plays here, and it also runs on its own , in English, Turkish and German, with a notebook at the bottom that lists every hidden thing in it. 
 Updated 15 September 2026

## Determinism does not buy you a forecast. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/notes/determinism/

If every decision is in principle knowable, is the financial future predictable? No, and the reason is structural.

Second note · August 2026 

## Determinism does not buy you a forecast
 The question this note comes from is old and the answer people reach for is usually wrong. If determinism is true, if every decision is in principle knowable from what came before it, does it follow that the financial future is predictable? The paper argues that it does not, and that the failure is structural rather than a shortfall of data or computing power. More data does not close this gap, because the gap is not made of missing data.
 The inference fails twice, at two different joints. The first is general: sensitive dependence on initial conditions, computational irreducibility, and the problem a predictor has predicting a system it is itself inside. The second is specific to markets: a forecast, once acted on, alters the thing it forecast; an informationally efficient market cannot exist, because nobody would pay to gather the information that made it efficient; and models shape the behaviour they claim to describe. None of this is mine. Even assembled well, it is a literature review and not a paper, and the note says so about itself. 
 What is left to claim comes from SIMEA. If agents are decision subjects steered by systems rather than autonomous optimisers, then how much of a behaviour is generated externally varies between agents, between markets and over time. Externally generated behaviour is by construction more forecastable, because it is a function of an input a modeller can in principle observe. That gives the first proposition: forecastability falls as the autonomy threshold rises and climbs as the influence gradient grows. Predictability stops being a property a market has or lacks and becomes a coordinate it sits at. 
 That reframes the original question rather than answering it yes or no. Predictability was never a consequence of determinism. It is a consequence of influence. A world can be fully deterministic and unforecastable, and a world can be indeterministic in its foundations and highly forecastable at the level where the steering happens. And there is a second proposition that will not leave the first alone: predictability produced by systemic influence is arbitraged away once it is identified, which pushes influence architectures to escalate, to steer harder in order to keep producing it. 
 The note is a positioning note and there is no draft yet, which is the accurate description of where it stands. It carries a section on what would sink the argument, written before anyone else could write it. And it carries the part I would want read first if only one section could be: the source check. Every reference was verified against a publisher or DOI level record, and ten needed correction. Then each source was checked for whether it actually says what the note claims it says. Six of twenty are done. Four of those claims held and two failed, both in the treatment of Popper and in that of Samuelson, and both are corrected in the note. Everybody claims rigour. The part worth publishing is the audit that found two of my own claims false. 
 The part worth publishing is the audit that found two of my own claims false. Source check 
 4 held 
 2 failed 
 14 not yet checked 
 Twenty sources in the note. Every one was verified against a publisher or DOI level record first, and ten needed correction. Six have since been checked for whether they say what the note says they say: four held and two did not. Both failures are corrected in the note. About

## The agent was never alone: SIMEA. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/notes/simea/

The agent as a decision subject, embedded in systems that steer it, and what that does to the idea of a preference.

First note · August 2026 

## The agent was never alone: SIMEA
 A research project I keep in the open. Classical economics models the agent as a rational maximiser; behavioural economics keeps the maximiser and catalogues its failures. SIMEA starts elsewhere: the agent as a decision subject, embedded in and steered by systems. Algorithms, platforms, recommender architectures. The framework proposes three measurable constructs: the influence gradient a system exerts on a choice, the autonomy threshold that remains the agent's own, and the entropy of the choice environment itself.
 A second note takes the framework seriously and asks what it implies for forecasting: if determinism holds, does it follow that financial futures are predictable? It argues that it does not, and that predictability is a function of autonomy. 
 About

## Agent Gateway. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/projects/agent-gateway/

A gateway that AI agents call tools through: an API contract compiled into signed mappings, every call decided by two policy engines before it leaves.

product 

## Agent Gateway
 A gateway that AI agents call tools through: an API contract compiled into signed mappings, every call decided by two policy engines before it leaves.

### Measured
 305 Go tests under race detection 
 34 governance policy tests 
 13 authorization cases 

### What holds
 Every decision names the bytes that produced it: the mapping version, the policy bundle, the spec hash. 
 A regenerated mapping cannot silently replace a working one. 
 Refuses what it cannot prove: an unsigned mapping, a tenant mismatch, a mutation without an idempotency key. 

### Where it stands
 Runs, with a two replica stack under Docker; the repository is private. 

### The door
 The product runs on a server, and this site has none. Behind the door is a sealed copy that opens with a password, in your browser. 
 Open the app

product 

## Frons
 Every photo of one person in an event set of thousands, from one selfie, without the face ever leaving their device.

### Measured
 36 489 faces in a 20 MB index of a 49 GB event 
 9 ms to search them on an iPhone 
 53 ms in a browser 

### What holds
 The same ONNX models on the server, the phone and the browser, so every vector lives in one space. 
 The server holds the index and is never told which face belongs to the person asking. 
 Every threshold came from a measurement, and the ones that could not be measured are off. 

### Where it stands
 Runs in the browser and as an iOS app over one server; nothing is published. 

### The door
 The product runs on a server, and this site has none. Behind the door is a sealed copy that opens with a password, in your browser.

 All Figures Reading The citations are left in the language they were read in. 

### Instruments

#### Four instruments, and what each of them refuses to do
 Carried over unchanged from unitguard, which names all four and picks none the unitguard case study on keremozdemir.de 

#### What CBAM will cost you, and what you still do not know
 Directive (EU) 2023/959 recital 46 and Article 10a(1a) of Directive 2003/87/EC eur-lex.europa.eu last read 2026 08 21 
 Sectors in scope from 1 January 2026. Cement, iron and steel, aluminium, fertilisers, electricity, hydrogen. European Commission, Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism_en last read 2026 08 21 
 De minimis threshold. 50 tonnes, cumulative net mass per importer per calendar year. Regulation (EU) 2025/2083, new Article 2(3a) and Annex VII point 1 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202502083 last read 2026 08 21 
 Goods outside the threshold. Electricity and hydrogen carry no de minimis relief at any volume. Mayer Brown and KPMG notes on Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 https://www.mayerbrown.com/en/insights/publications/2025/10/eu-adopts-cbam-simplification-regulation-10-key-amendments-and-challenges-ahead last read 2026 08 21 
 Effect of crossing the threshold. All CBAM obligations apply to the whole calendar year, not only to the excess above 50 tonnes. Climate Leadership Council, A Guide to the EU CBAM, April 2026 https://clcouncil.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/A-Guide-to-the-EU-CBAM.pdf last read 2026 08 21 
 Chargeable share of embedded emissions. 2.5 per cent in 2026 rising to 100 per cent in 2034, being 100 per cent minus the CBAM factor on free allocation. Directive (EU) 2023/959 recital 46, Article 10a(1a) of Directive 2003/87/EC https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023L0959 last read 2026 08 21 
 Free allocation adjustment mechanism. Certificates are reduced by the free allocation embedded in the good, set out in a dedicated implementing act. Article 31 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2620 https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism/cbam-legislation-and-guidance_en last read 2026 08 21 
 Sale of certificates begins. 1 February 2027. Article 20 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202502083 last read 2026 08 21 
 First annual declaration. 30 September 2027, for imports made in 2026, and 30 September each year after. Article 6 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2025/2083 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=OJ:L_202502083 last read 2026 08 21 
 Quarterly certificate holding. At least 50 per cent of cumulative embedded emissions, reduced from 80 per cent. Article 22 as amended, per Mayer Brown and KPMG notes https://kpmg.com/pl/en/insights/law/legal-alert-cbam-mechanism-revised-key-changes-in-eu-regulation-2025-2083.html last read 2026 08 21 
 Penalty, authorised declarant. Equal to the EU ETS excess emissions penalty of EUR 100 per tonne under Article 16(3) of Directive 2003/87/EC, indexed under Article 16(4), for each certificate not surrendered. The indexed amount for a given year is not stated in this tool. Article 26(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023R0956 last read 2026 08 21 
 Penalty, importing over the threshold without authorisation. Three to five times the standard penalty, reported as EUR 300 to EUR 500 per tonne, reducible where the threshold is exceeded by no more than 10 per cent. Article 26(2) as amended, per Mayer Brown note https://www.mayerbrown.com/en/insights/publications/2025/10/eu-adopts-cbam-simplification-regulation-10-key-amendments-and-challenges-ahead last read 2026 08 21 
 Carbon price paid in the country of origin. Deductible. A declarant may claim a reduction in the number of certificates to reflect a carbon price effectively paid, net of any rebate or compensation, with evidence. Article 9 of Regulation (EU) 2023/956 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:32023R0956 last read 2026 08 21 
 Basis of the certificate price. Set by the Commission from EU ETS auction prices. Quarterly average for 2026 imports, weekly average from 2027. European Commission, CBAM definitive regime, and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/2548 https://taxation-customs.ec.europa.eu/carbon-border-adjustment-mechanism/cbam-definitive-regime_en last read 2026 08 21 
 Indicative EU ETS allowance price offered as a starting value. EUR 74.04 per tonne CO2e, monthly average for May 2026. Editable, and not a live price. Initiativ, The Carbon Benchmark in 2026, quoting IndexBox https://www.takeinitiativ.com/articles/carbon-benchmark last read 2026 08 21 
 Scope extension to downstream goods. Proposed 17 December 2025, procedure 2025/0419(COD), proposed to apply from 2028. Still a proposal at this date, without force, and excluded from the pricing here. European Parliament legislative observatory https://oeil.europarl.europa.eu/oeil/en/document-summary?id=1879956 last read 2026 08 21 

#### A target is one number
 Science Based Targets initiative, Absolute Contraction Approach. The binding text is the SBTi Corporate Near-Term Criteria, version 5.3.1, April 2026 sciencebasedtargets.org last read 2026 08 25 

### Economics you can play with

#### The evolution of cooperation
 The first tournament: fourteen submitted programs plus a random one, two hundred rounds per pairing, payoffs of five, three, one and zero for temptation, reward, punishment and sucker. Tit for tat, submitted by Anatol Rapoport, finished first. The tournament was run five times to smooth out the random element. Anatol Rapoport, Darryl A. Seale and Andrew M. Colman, Is Tit for Tat the Answer? On the Con

## Interactive economics, the model in the page. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/work/essays/

Four pieces of economics with the model in the page: why a used car market collapses, who really pays a tax, why the future is worth less than today.

04 4   pieces 

## Economics
 01 Lemons Adverse selection, run as a used car market. Set the spread of quality and how much buyers can see. 02 Incidence Drag the supply and demand curves, set a tax, and watch the burden split between the two sides. 03 Discounting Move the rate and watch a fixed benefit in a distant year lose almost all of its present value. 04 Cooperation The repeated prisoner's dilemma. Pick the strategies, set the payoffs and the chance the game continues. Case studies

## Game theory. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/work/games/

Six small games that are played rather than read: the beauty contest, the commons, the long game, matching pennies, the stag hunt and the ultimatum.

06 6   pieces 

## Game theory
 01 The Long Game Why a future changes the arithmetic of the present. 20 to 30 min 02 The Stag Hunt The trap is doubt rather than greed. Two equilibria, and only one of them is good. 5 to 10 min 03 The Ultimatum Fairness as a force in real bargaining rather than a preference. 5 to 10 min 04 The Commons The tragedy as a result about rules rather than about people. 8 to 12 min 05 The Beauty Contest How deep you should reason about other people. 5 to 8 min 06 Matching Pennies Sometimes the only unexploitable strategy is to be unpredictable. 5 to 10 min Case studies

### Where the code lives
 esg-toolkit last push 2026-09-22 Carbon decomposition, target pathways, abatement cost and CBAM embedded emissions. Three of the five instruments come from here. 
 analyst-toolkit last push 2026-09-22 Market sizing from two directions, and a discounted cash flow with the terminal value taken apart. 
 unitguard last push 2026-09-22 Unit and dimension safety for energy and emissions arithmetic. It refuses rather than guesses. 
 open-climate-data last push 2026-09-22 One interface over public climate, energy and emissions datasets, where every value carries its source, its version and its date. 
 simea research, CC BY 4.0 for the writing last push 2026-09-22 The framework note and the positioning note, with the models that test them. Neither has been peer reviewed and the repository says so. 
 rota last push 2026-09-24 The routing layer over the skill packs, and the only repository here with a runtime. 
 agent-kit and eleven more last push 2026-09-21 Twelve repositories of working method packaged as skills, one per trade: finance, sustainability, research, writing, risk, strategy, presentations, spreadsheets, careers, sites, repositories, and the conventions the other eleven follow. 
 keremozdemirra.github.io this site, as it is served last push 2026-09-24 This site, as it is served. Nothing is compiled out of reach: what a browser receives is what the repository holds.

## Free CBAM and emissions calculators, in the browser. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/work/instruments/

The kind of arithmetic that otherwise takes a spreadsheet, a consultant, or both: CBAM, embedded emissions, reduction pathways, provenance and valuation.

05 5   pieces 

## Instruments
 CBAM Running Whether an importer has to report under CBAM at all, and what the certificates cost if they do. 
 Embedded emissions Running How much carbon is inside a product by the time it is finished, traced back through everything that went into it. 
 Pathway Running A reduction target, and the total carbon it still lets you emit on the way there, which is the part a target leaves out. 
 Provenance Running An emission factor that carries where it came from, and keeps carrying it through every calculation it enters. 
 Analyst Running A valuation that shows how much of its answer rests on a guess about the far future, and a market sized from two directions at once. 
 
 Arrow keys run an instrument in the panel beside the list, and Enter opens the running one on its own page.

### CBAM
 live in this panel type in it 

#### What CBAM will cost you, and what you still do not know
 Enter what you import: this prices the certificates from your own figures and names the ones you are still missing. 
 
 01 Year and carbon price Year of import 2026 2027 2028 2029 2030 2031 2032 2033 2034 Carbon price, EUR per tonne CO2e Indicative, so replace it with the figure your treasury uses. 74.04 EUR , monthly average for May 2026, read on 2026-08-21 
 Chargeable share for this year : 2.5 % · free allocation still standing : 97.5 %

 countable net mass against a threshold of 50 t 
 Over the threshold: every CBAM obligation then applies to the whole calendar year, the first 50 tonnes included.
 04 Embedded emissions and data gaps 249.7 t CO2e 
 from the lines that carry a supplier figure
 1 . Calcined clay 228 t CO2e · 5.7 t chargeable 
 3 . Cement 21.7 t CO2e · 0.54 t chargeable 
 These lines carry no specific embedded emissions figure, so nothing is computed for them: a default would produce a total assembled out of guesses.
 2 . Unwrought aluminium 40 t · Ask the operator of the installation in China for the specific embedded emissions of this good, in tonnes CO2e per tonne. 
 05 Indicative certificate cost 455.68 EUR 
 Chargeable emissions 249.7 × 2.5 % = 6.24 t CO2e 
 At the price entered 6.24 × 74.04 = 462.19 EUR 
 Less carbon price already paid at origin 6.51 EUR 
 This covers only the lines that carry an emissions figure, so it is not your bill while 1 line(s) are still missing one.
 06 The constants this rests on Every figure the arithmetic uses, with where it was read from and when.

## Agent based models that run in the browser. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/work/simulations/

Five models where a rule everybody follows on their own produces a result nobody chose: a neighbourhood that sorts itself, a rumour crossing a network.

05 5   pieces 

## Simulations
 01 Segregation A runnable Schelling model. A mild individual preference turning into a segregated map. 02 Diffusion The same contagion at the same transmission probability, run over three network shapes: a lattice, a small world graph and a scale free graph. 03 Jam A ring road with nothing blocking it. Set the density and the reaction time, tap one brake. 04 Pile A sandpile driven one grain at a time, organising itself to the edge of stability. 05 Recommender A feed that decides what each agent sees, run again against a neutral one on the same population. Case studies

## Tools. Kerem Özdemir

URL: https://keremozdemir.de/work/workshop/

Nine jobs that otherwise need paid software or a hand-built spreadsheet, each one a tool that opens in a browser, held up by 466 checks written by hand.

09 9   pieces 

## Tools
 01 Dotsheet Text into Unified English Braille, and the braille back into text, so you can read what it actually says. 58   checks 02 Sheetwise Puts the pages of a PDF onto press sheets in the order a folded and stitched book needs. 72   checks 03 Cutplan Turns a drawing into instructions for a laser cutter, cutting the holes before the outline so the part does not drop out first. 45   checks 04 Loudmeter Measures how loud an audio file is against the broadcast standard, and says how much to turn it up or down. 36   checks 05 Cutfill How much earth has to come out and how much has to go in to bring a site to the level you want. 45   checks 06 Cuecheck Checks a subtitle file against the reading speed and timing rules a broadcaster applies. 69   checks 07 Boardplan Lays parts out on sheet material in cuts a panel saw can actually make. 37   checks 08 Buildup The layers of a wall in, how much heat it loses out, to the standard building control asks for. 40   checks 09 Costcurve Ranks emission cuts by what each one costs per tonne, and will not cut more than there is to cut. 64   checks Case studies
